scenes.say: Does mak-kee-ah-toh mean coffee with milk? Not quite, and the real meaning explains the drink.

scenes.title: It means stained.
scenes.say: In Italian, mak-kee-ah-toh means stained or marked. So a caf-feh mak-kee-ah-toh is literally a stained coffee.
What gets stained? The espresso. A small spot of milk leaves a mark on top, which is why the drink stays mostly coffee.

scenes.title: Same word, flipped.
scenes.say: A latte mak-kee-ah-toh is the reverse. It is mostly steamed milk with a little espresso, so the coffee is the mark this time.

scenes.title: At the bar.
scenes.say: If you ask for a mak-kee-ah-toh, you will usually get espresso with a spot of milk. For the milky glass, say latte mak-kee-ah-toh.
So mak-kee-ah-toh means marked, not milky. Coffee marked with milk, or milk marked with coffee. Save this for your next order.
